sentences.text: This dinosaur is known from a partial skeleton preserved in a death pose, with its head positioned above its torso.
The specimen lacks most of the forelimbs, the pectoral girdle, the distal hindlimbs, and the majority of the tail.
Its skull is crushed and tilted to show the left side, measuring 185 mm in length.
Small stones discovered inside its chest cavity suggest it swallowed gastroliths to help digest food.
The fossils were unearthed from river deposits in western Liaoning Province, China.
This single-species genus sits phylogenetically between Pelecanimimus polyodon and Harpymimus oklandikovi.
Shenzhousaurus lived between 125.77 and 119.57 million years ago during the Barremian to Aptian stages.
